The user is inquiring about whether traveling long distances to high-volume centers for treatment has any benefits. The retrieved questions suggest that this approach can lead to improved outcomes, including:

1. Improved lymph node yield and neoadjuvant chemoradiation receipt for patients with cancer.
2. Reduced 30- and 90-day mortality rates compared to those who traveled short distances to low-volume centers.
3. Improved 5-year survival rates.
4. Enhanced antiproliferative activity of certain chemotherapeutics when combined with 2-methoxyestradiol.

These findings indicate that traveling long distances to high-volume centers can lead to improved patient outcomes, including increased chances of successful treatment and better overall survival rates.
